system:
You are the reading pass of an illustration engine. You read one large division of a work (a whole text such as a scripture, a novel or a story collection) and return its skeleton as JSON. The engine later draws pictures of the text's moments, so for every stretch of text it needs to know who is on stage and where, and it needs a draft brief for illustrators.

The text comes as numbered units. Each unit line starts with its id (for example `17:4` or `[12]`). Lines starting with `##` are headings, not units.

Return:

1. characters: one entry per individual (a person, a being, or an animal that acts) who appears in or is named in the text.
   - One individual is one entry, even when the text uses different names, titles or descriptions for them. List every form in `aliases`: other names, nicknames, titles, descriptions, and disguises or assumed names.
   - Different individuals who share a name or a title get separate entries, one each. Never fold two people into one entry because they share a name. When a title passes from one holder to another (a ruler dies or is succeeded, an office changes hands), the new holder is a new entry. The `note` must say in one line who this is and how to tell them apart from anyone else with the same name: whose child, spouse or servant they are, their role, and where in the text they appear.
   - A disguised, renamed or unnamed person who the text later identifies is the same entry as their named self, with the disguise or description in `aliases`. If you suspect two entries are one individual but the text does not settle it, keep both and set `same_person_as` on the less certain one to the other's id; otherwise set it to "".
   - Skip people who occur only inside a list of names (a genealogy or roster) and never act.
   - Add a group (an army, a crowd, a household) only when it acts as one on stage, with kind "group".
2. locations: one entry per place where action happens, with aliases and a one-line note. Include places the text refers to only by description ("the sea", "the valley", "the house") when the context shows which place it is, under the place's proper name if the work gives one anywhere.
3. sections: split the text into story sections, runs of consecutive units that tell one episode, the way a study edition's headings or a novel's scenes do. Start a new section when the time, the place or the main action changes. Every unit belongs to exactly one section; sections are in order, with no gaps and no overlaps. This division has 810 units. Aim for roughly 45 sections (36 to 54), averaging about 18 units each; some sections will be much shorter and some longer. Never split one continuous scene, conversation or battle, but do split long speeches, lists, sets of instructions and law codes wherever the topic changes. Give the ids of each section's first and last unit and a short title. For each section:
   - setting: ids of the locations where its action happens.
   - on_stage: ids of every character present in the section's action, whether the section names them or only refers to them by a pronoun, a title or a description, or does not mention them but they are clearly there.
   - mentioned_only: ids of characters the section names or refers to who are not present.
4. brief: a draft brief for illustrators, for this division only. It holds only what is true across the whole division or a whole stretch of its world: one person or place is described in the cast, not here, and one episode's look belongs to its section, not here.
   - tone: one line on the mood the pictures should carry.
   - depiction_rules: a short list of how certain things in this text may or may not be shown, drawn from the text and from what you know about the work.
   - era: the stretch of the world this division is set in: a name, its people (who lives there and what they look like), dress, buildings and objects, and technology (what exists and what does not yet exist).
   Keep the brief under 200 words.

Use short, stable snake_case ids (for example `david`, `the_queen`, `main_street`). Section entries may only use ids from your own characters and locations lists. Do not quote the text.

characters.name: Elkanah
characters.note: Ephraimite husband of Hannah and Peninnah, father of Samuel; goes yearly to Shiloh to sacrifice (ch. 1-2).

characters.name: Hannah
characters.note: Elkanah's wife, barren, who prays for a son and gives Samuel to Yahweh at Shiloh (ch. 1-2).

characters.name: Peninnah
characters.note: Elkanah's other wife, mother of many children, who provokes Hannah (ch. 1).

characters.name: Eli
characters.note: Old priest at Shiloh, father of Hophni and Phinehas, who judges Israel forty years and dies on hearing of the ark's capture (ch. 1-4).

characters.name: Samuel
characters.note: Son of Hannah, raised at Shiloh under Eli; becomes prophet and judge who anoints Saul and David (ch. 1-28).

characters.name: Hophni
characters.note: Wicked son of Eli, priest at Shiloh, killed in battle with the ark (ch. 2, 4).

characters.name: Phinehas
characters.note: Wicked son of Eli, priest at Shiloh, killed in battle; not to be confused with later Phinehas (ch. 2, 4).

characters.name: Phinehas's wife
characters.note: Wife of Eli's son Phinehas; names her son Ichabod on hearing of the ark's loss and dies in childbirth (ch. 4).

characters.name: Ichabod
characters.note: Son of Phinehas's wife, named for the departed glory (ch. 4).

characters.name: Dagon
characters.note: Philistine god whose image falls before the ark in Ashdod (ch. 5).

characters.name: Yahweh
characters.note: God of Israel, speaking and acting throughout; appears as speaker and actor in the narrative (all chapters).

characters.name: Philistine lords
characters.note: Rulers of the five Philistine cities who consult about the ark and gather in councils (ch. 5-6, 29).

characters.name: Ark of Yahweh
characters.note: The sacred ark moved between Shiloh, Ebenezer, Ashdod, Gath, Ekron, Beth Shemesh and Kiriath Jearim; a central object (ch. 4-7).

characters.name: Men of Ashdod
characters.note: Philistine townsmen struck with tumors when the ark is brought to them (ch. 5).

characters.name: Men of Beth Shemesh
characters.note: Israelite town that receives the ark on a cart and is struck for looking into it (ch. 6).

characters.name: Elders of Israel
characters.note: Israelite leaders who ask Samuel for a king and gather for war (ch. 4, 8, 10-11).

characters.name: Kish
characters.note: Benjamite whose donkeys are lost; father of Saul (ch. 9-10).

characters.name: Saul
characters.note: First king of Israel, son of Kish, anointed by Samuel; rejected by Yahweh; dies on Mount Gilboa (ch. 9-31).

characters.name: Saul's servant
characters.note: Servant who accompanies Saul to find the donkeys and to Samuel (ch. 9).

characters.name: Saul's uncle
characters.note: Uncle of Saul who asks where Saul has been (ch. 10).

characters.name: Young women at the city
characters.note: Girls drawing water who direct Saul to Samuel (ch. 9).

characters.name: Band of prophets
characters.note: Group of prophets Saul meets near Gibeah of God (ch. 10, 19).

characters.name: Nahash
aliases: the king of the children of Ammon
characters.note: Ammonite king who besieges Jabesh Gilead (ch. 11-12).

characters.name: Men of Jabesh Gilead
characters.note: Besieged town whose elders bargain with Nahash and are rescued by Saul (ch. 11).

characters.name: Worthless fellows
characters.note: Men who despise Saul after his election and bring no tribute (ch. 10).

characters.name: Jonathan
characters.note: Son of Saul, friend and covenant partner of David; struck the Philistine garrison at Geba (ch. 13-20, 31).

characters.name: Jonathan's armor bearer
aliases: the young man who bore his armor
characters.note: Armor bearer who joins Jonathan's attack on the Philistine garrison (ch. 14).

characters.name: Philistine garrison
characters.note: Philistine troops at Michmash and Geba who are attacked by Jonathan (ch. 13-14).

characters.name: Ahijah
characters.note: Priest with Saul at Gibeah who wears the ephod; son of Ahitub, descendant of Eli (ch. 14).

characters.name: Agag
characters.note: Amalekite king spared by Saul and cut in pieces by Samuel at Gilgal (ch. 15).

characters.name: Amalekites
characters.note: Enemy people to be destroyed; attacked by Saul and later by David at Ziklag (ch. 15, 27, 30).

characters.name: Kenites
characters.note: People who showed kindness to Israel and are spared by Saul (ch. 15).

characters.name: Jesse
characters.note: Father of eight sons including David, of Bethlehem (ch. 16-17).

characters.name: Eliab
characters.note: Eldest son of Jesse; rebukes David at the battle lines and is passed over by Samuel (ch. 16-17).

characters.name: Abinadab
characters.note: Son of Jesse passed over by Samuel; a brother of David (ch. 16-17).

characters.name: Shammah
characters.note: Son of Jesse passed over by Samuel; a brother of David (ch. 16-17).

characters.name: David
characters.note: Youngest son of Jesse, anointed by Samuel; harpist, armor bearer and slayer of Goliath; fugitive from Saul and later king of Judah (ch. 16-31).

characters.name: Goliath
characters.note: Philistine champion from Gath, killed by David with a sling (ch. 17).

characters.name: Goliath's shield bearer
aliases: the man who bore the shield
characters.note: Shield bearer walking before Goliath (ch. 17).

characters.name: Abner
characters.note: Saul's cousin and army captain; presents David to Saul and is rebuked at night (ch. 14, 17, 20, 26).

characters.name: Merab
characters.note: Saul's elder daughter promised to David but given to Adriel (ch. 14, 18).

characters.name: Michal
characters.note: Saul's younger daughter who loves David, becomes his wife, and helps him escape (ch. 14, 18-19, 25).

characters.name: Women singers
characters.note: Women who sing of Saul's and David's victories (ch. 18).

characters.name: Evil spirit from Yahweh

characters.name: Saul's servants
characters.note: Servants who counsel Saul and carry out his orders (ch. 16-19).

characters.name: Adriel
characters.note: Man to whom Merab is given as wife (ch. 18).

characters.name: Ahimelech
characters.note: Priest at Nob who gives David bread and Goliath's sword and is killed by Saul's order (ch. 21-22).

characters.name: Doeg
characters.note: Edomite herdsman of Saul who reports David to Saul and kills the priests of Nob (ch. 21-22).

characters.name: Achish
characters.note: King of Gath who receives David and gives him Ziklag (ch. 21, 27-29).

characters.name: Gad
characters.note: Prophet who advises David to leave the stronghold (ch. 22).

characters.name: Abiathar
characters.note: Surviving son of Ahimelech who flees to David and carries the ephod (ch. 22-23, 30).

characters.name: David's men
characters.note: Band of outlaws and debtors who follow David (ch. 22-30).

characters.name: Ziphites
characters.note: Men of Ziph who betray David's hiding places to Saul (ch. 23, 26).

characters.name: Nabal
characters.note: Wealthy surly man of Carmel who insults David; dies ten days after (ch. 25).

characters.name: Abigail
characters.note: Intelligent wife of Nabal who pleads with David and then becomes his wife (ch. 25, 27, 30).

characters.name: Abishai
characters.note: David's nephew who offers to kill Saul in the camp (ch. 26).

characters.name: Ahinoam of Jezreel
characters.note: One of David's wives taken at Ziklag and rescued (ch. 25, 27, 30).

characters.name: Palti
characters.note: Man to whom Saul gave Michal (ch. 25).

characters.name: Woman of Endor
aliases: the woman with a familiar spirit
characters.note: Medium at Endor who raises Samuel's spirit for Saul (ch. 28).

characters.name: Egyptian servant
characters.note: Egyptian servant abandoned by Amalekites who guides David to their camp (ch. 30).

characters.name: Saul's armor bearer
characters.note: Armor bearer who refuses to kill Saul and then dies on his own sword (ch. 31).

characters.name: Valiant men of Jabesh Gilead
characters.note: Men who recover Saul's body from Beth Shan and bury it at Jabesh (ch. 31).

characters.name: Philistines
characters.note: Philistine army and people in the wars against Israel (throughout).

characters.name: Israelite army
characters.note: Israelite army and people in the battles (throughout).
